clue.text: True — men are stupid to pay

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words have been jumbled foolishly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical claim that men are foolish enough to hand over money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' signals an anagram of TRUE MEN ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay someone for work is to reward them financially, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Cause of food inspectors visiting 'Rising Sun'?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: Health inspectors call at a restaurant called the Rising Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising Sun' looks like a pub or restaurant name; read as wordplay, 'Rising' reverses STAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermin such as rodents in a kitchen would prompt a visit from health inspectors, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: A taste of apartment holidays?

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is taken from part of the following words

explanation.surface: A brief experience of renting flats for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'apartment' and 'holidays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Menthol is a minty flavour, so it is one particular taste.

clue.text: Guard's twisty thing on timer making all nervous initially

indicators.note: twisty means the word thing is twisted into a new order

parts.note: a watch is a timer worn on the wrist

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of making, all and nervous

explanation.surface: A sentry's coiled device on a clock puts everyone on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisty' rearranges THING to NIGHT; the first letters of 'making all nervous' give MAN. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A night watchman is a person employed to keep watch over premises after dark, a kind of security guard.

clue.text: Concerned with criminal trial to secure end of rogue trader

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to

indicators.note: to secure means to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other
criminal suggests the word trial is corrupted into another order
end of takes the last letter of rogue

explanation.surface: A dishonest merchant faces a criminal trial over his dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue trader' reads as one phrase, but 'rogue' only supplies its last letter; the definition is 'trader' alone. The anagram of the trial gives TAILR.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells goods to the public is a trader of a particular sort.

clue.text: Beat heartless hunky star

indicators.note: heartless here literally means the word heart is removed

parts.note: a heart-throb is an attractive celebrity idol

explanation.surface: A handsome celebrity shown as cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a description of the star, but it removes HEART from HEARTTHROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, the same as a beat of the heart.

clue.text: Hurried outlay with no end of pain

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: outlay is money spent, a spend

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of pain

explanation.surface: Rushed spending that comes without any pain at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes N, the last letter of 'pain', from SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, meaning went quickly or rushed.

clue.text: Parking help not on, but given compensation

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
aid means help
off is the opposite of on, as with a switch

explanation.surface: A motorist finds no parking assistance but is reimbursed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid off describes someone settled with money, often to end employment, so recompensed.

clue.text: Decline of French taxonomic groups — those without heart

parts.note: de is French for of
genera are the groups between family and species in biological classification

indicators.note: without heart drops the middle letters of those, leaving its outer pair

explanation.surface: A decline among French biological classifications, with some lacking a centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To degenerate is to deteriorate or worsen, a synonym of the verb decline.

clue.text: Working in firm for the next retirement opportunity?

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside another

parts.note: tight means firm or secure
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: An employee wonders when the company will next let them retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work for good; here it means going to bed, so the next chance is this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed, and the next opportunity for that is this coming evening.

clue.text: Stretching and breaking with the top off

indicators.note: with the top off removes the first letter, the top of a word in this sense

parts.note: cracking means breaking or splitting

explanation.surface: Pulling something taut until it snaps, its upper part gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the top off' removes C from CRACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack was a torture device that pulled a body apart, so racking is pulling or straining.

clue.text: Wears the trousers, as a film director does

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being the one in charge, especially in a household
a director literally decides which camera takes to film and orders them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to be in control, and a director literally gives orders for each filmed take.

clue.text: Form of transport highly subject to inflation

definitions.text: Form of transport highly subject to inflation

parts.words: Form of transport highly subject to inflation
parts.note: inflation reads as rising prices, but this craft is literally inflated and rises high in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests rising fares; the vehicle itself is filled with heated gas and flies high.
explanation.definitionFit: This aircraft is an envelope filled with heated gas, so it must be blown up and it travels high.

clue.text: This scam goes wrong, Nick discovered, becoming fractious

indicators.note: goes wrong means the letters of this scam end up in a mistaken order
discovered means uncovered, the outer letters of Nick stripped away

explanation.surface: A swindle fails and a petty thief is caught, turning unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges THIS SCAM to SCHISMAT; 'discovered' strips Nick to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Schismatic describes a group prone to splitting into factions, so divisive and quarrelsome.

clue.text: Served local wine, getting nicked

indicators.note: served as in dished up, so the word local is presented in a new arrangement

parts.note: red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: A drinker is given the house wine and then gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' rearranges LOCAL to COLLA. 'nicked' is British slang for arrested, not stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Collared is slang for arrested, caught by the police who grab the suspect.

clue.text: Invite king inside since in favour

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the others

parts.note: as can mean since, as in as it was late
for means in favour of
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Bringing the monarch indoors because he is popular.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for someone is to request their presence, much like inviting them.

clue.text: Up to now the girl's almost top, after strike

indicators.note: after places the strike first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: to hit is to strike
her is the possessive for the girl

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A girl's top so far has nearly been ruined after a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning until this point in time, so far.

clue.text: Effect of bill on Independent Member of Parliament

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the bill comes second, following the politician

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent in politics
a bill becomes an act when passed by parliament

explanation.surface: An independent MP's proposed law has some consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the influence or result something has, a synonym for effect.

clue.text: Part of race to get Stones number one?

parts.note: pits are the stones of fruit such as cherries
top means best, number one

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones reaching the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' and 'number one' suggest the band and the charts; they are fruit pits and TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, a halt in the pits to refuel or change tyres is a part of the race.

clue.text: Euphoric experiences with marijuana — a most memorable thing!

parts.note: highs are feelings of euphoria
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Getting high on cannabis is called an unforgettable experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A high spot is the outstanding moment of an event, its best or most memorable part.

clue.text: I am covered in glue — it's my hobby

indicators.note: covered in means one piece is surrounded by another

parts.note: paste is a type of glue
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A crafter, smeared in adhesive, declares that sticking things is a favourite pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is an activity done for pleasure in spare time, a synonym of hobby.

clue.text: Revolutionary Amish promotes complete change

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters of Amish promotes being turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A radical among the Amish advocates total transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamorphosis is a transformation, as of caterpillar into butterfly, a full change of form.

clue.text: Right, step up and summarise

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Instructions to move right, quicken, and then sum up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step up' looks like a phrase to increase; 'up' reverses PACE to ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, going over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Language skills must take a long time

indicators.note: must take suggests the answer is taken from within the words that come before

explanation.surface: Learning a foreign tongue is a slow business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal way to say a very lengthy period, as in waiting for an eternity.

clue.text: Enormous insectivorous bird — a new finch, oddly

parts.note: the tit is a small bird that feeds on insects

indicators.note: oddly means some alternate letters of finch are dropped, keeping the others

explanation.surface: A huge insect-eating bird turns out to be a strange new finch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' removes the odd letters of 'finch', leaving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of colossal size, like the mythical Titans of ancient Greek legend.

clue.text: Cheating giant red ruler?

parts.note: the red kangaroo is the largest kangaroo, and roo is short for kangaroo
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A huge red-faced monarch with a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giant red' seems to describe a ruler; it is the red kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, so rooking is defrauding.

clue.text: Egyptian quietly lying in bed?

indicators.note: lying in means one piece rests inside another

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A native of Egypt resting silently in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt is a member of the native Christian community of Egypt.

clue.text: New plush store puts covers on chairs

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of plush store are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A recently opened furnishing shop re-covers seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholsterer fits padding and fabric to furniture, so it reupholsters seats.
